newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean blue chips end lower in paltry trade.
newsitem.headline: Chilean blue chips end lower in paltry trade.

text.p: Chilean shares closed softer with volume reduced to token turnover as the result of Wall Street's closure for the Labor Day holiday, said traders.
The bolsa's opening direction will depend mainly on whether the number of orders swells or remains slack, they said.
"If volume improves, then we could see the market making a light recovery," said one dealer.
The 40-share IPSA index ended down 0.2 percent at 95.87 points. The general IGPA index declined 0.25 percent to 5,289.47 points.
Volume fell to 5 billion pesos from 11.3 billion Friday.
With foreign investors on holiday and institutional investors remaining on the sidelines, the only buy orders were from brokers themselves or small private players, said traders.
"With such small turnover it is impossible to define any clear trend," said one dealer.

Decliners included Chile's largest paper maker CMPC on remarks from company president Ernesto Ayala that the firm's earnings will be down 40 percent this year on 1995 as the result of lower wood pulp prices, said traders.
CMPC ended off 1.36 percent at 5,080 pesos.
Other losers included copper products company Madeco, down 1.08 percent at 920 pesos and brewery CCU which lost 0.87 percent to 1,590 pesos.
Winners included state power utility Colbun, up 1.57 percent at 48 pesos, forestry firm Masisa, up 1.28 percent at 197-1/2 pesos and electricity firm Enersis which rose 0.1 percent to 248-3/4 pesos.
